patient_overview.name: Abdul Kshlerin
patient_overview.description: Abdul Kshlerin is a 66-year-old man from Rockaway, New Jersey, who has lived with heart problems for most of his adult life, including a mechanical aortic valve replacement in 2019 and ongoing ischemic heart disease. He works full-time, lives in a crowded household of seven, and comes across as guarded and quiet in the exam room, answering in short sentences until a question is asked twice. He has decided he's ready to make one concrete change to his eating but isn't sure where to start, and he tends to downplay how much he relies on takeout and comfort eating to get through stressful days.

demographics.occupation: Maintenance technician at a commercial office building
demographics.cultural_context: Abdul grew up working-class in northern New Jersey, left school after his GED to start working, and has always measured a good day by whether he kept busy and provided for his family. Food was never a big ritual in his house growing up—whoever got home first ate. As an adult, grabbing a meal on the way home or ordering in became both convenience and the main way he unwinds and connects with coworkers and his wife. He doesn't talk much about feelings, but he'll talk about where to get a decent sandwich.
